handoff.reportSection:
## Starter analytics dashboard

Created [Analytics basics (wizard)](https://us.posthog.com/project/763999/dashboard/2405202) with three starter views:

- Storefront pageviews over the last 30 days
- Total shop error retry clicks over the last 30 days
- Daily trend of shop error retry clicks

The dashboard and all insights are tagged `wizard` and will populate as the integration receives browser events.

handoff.goals: Configure PostHog log capture for the supported Next.js server runtime using the documented OTLP approach, without exporting pre-existing application logs.
handoff.did: Created `instrumentation.ts` with a dedicated `LoggerProvider`, PostHog OTLP HTTP exporter, resource service name, and a development-only server warning when either `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` is unavailable. The provider is used directly rather than registered globally, so no pre-existing loggers or outputs are exported or changed. Updated `src/lib/api.ts` to emit only two integration-added, structured records through this dedicated logger: `Product listing loaded` (INFO, endpoint and product count) after a successful product fetch and `Product listing request failed` (ERROR, endpoint and status) on a non-success response. These records support filtering storefront product-list availability and failures in PostHog Logs without sending request data, secrets, or user data.
handoff.forNextAgent: Install the required OpenTelemetry packages before building or typechecking: `@opentelemetry/sdk-logs`, `@opentelemetry/exporter-logs-otlp-http`, `@opentelemetry/api-logs`, and `@opentelemetry/resources`. Do not change their versions unless resolving against an existing OTel setup; this project had no pre-existing OTel packages. The existing public environment keys `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` are used by the server exporter and were confirmed present. With the products API running, load the storefront page to produce `Product listing loaded`; make its `/v1/products` response non-OK to produce `Product listing request failed`, then find those messages in PostHog Logs. Delivery remains unverified until observed. Only records added in this task are exported. If the app later has existing OpenTelemetry global loggers that the user explicitly wants exported too, add `logs.setGlobalLoggerProvider(loggerProvider)` in `register()` (and import `logs` from `@opentelemetry/api-logs`); do not use that change for console or unrelated logging without that request.
handoff.evidence: Read the installed `logs-nextjs` skill and its Next.js OTLP reference, then read back both edited files. Confirmed `package.json` has Next.js 16.4.6 and no OpenTelemetry packages, and source inspection found no existing logger or OTel setup. Confirmed both required public environment-key names are present through `check_env_keys`. No build, lint, or typecheck was run because the task requires dependency installation to be left for review and the OpenTelemetry imports are not installed yet.
handoff.assumptions: The server-rendered dynamic product listing runs in the default Node.js runtime, as there is no edge-runtime configuration. The public PostHog host environment value is the correct regional ingestion base supplied by upstream configuration.
handoff.conflict: OpenTelemetry dependencies are intentionally not added to the manifest or lockfile in this task and must be installed during review.
